content.title: What are Method References?
content.description: Method References, introduced in Java 8, provide a shorthand syntax for referring to existing methods using the :: operator, making code more readable and concise.

content.content: Sometimes a Lambda Expression simply calls an existing method without adding any additional logic. In such cases, Java allows developers to replace the lambda with a Method Reference. Method references improve readability while reducing boilerplate code and work seamlessly with functional interfaces and the Streams API.

content.title: Why Use Method References?
content.content: Method references simplify lambda expressions, improve code readability, encourage code reuse, and integrate naturally with functional programming features introduced in Java 8.
Method Reference Syntax
A method reference uses the double-colon (::) operator to refer to an existing method instead of writing an equivalent lambda expression.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Use a method reference when a lambda expression only calls an existing method without additional processing.

content.content: Lambda vs Method Reference
Method references provide a cleaner alternative when the lambda expression simply delegates execution to another method.
Types of Method References
Java supports four different kinds of method references depending on what is being referenced.
Static Method Reference
A static method reference points to a static method of a class.
Instance Method Reference
An instance method reference points to a method belonging to a specific object or any object of a particular class.
Constructor Reference
Constructor references provide a concise way to create new objects without explicitly calling constructors inside lambda expressions.

content.title: Constructor Reference Example
content.code:
Supplier<List<String>> listSupplier = ArrayList::new;

List<String> list = listSupplier.get();

content.content: Method References with Streams
Method references are widely used in Streams API operations such as map(), filter(), and forEach() to make pipelines shorter and easier to understand.
Advantages & Limitations
Applications

items.question: Streams API
items.answer: Used with map(), filter(), sorted(), and forEach().

items.question: Event Handling
items.answer: Passing existing methods as event handlers.

items.question: Functional Programming
items.answer: Simplifying Lambda Expressions throughout Java applications.

content.content: Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Using a Contact Shortcut
content.content: Instead of typing someone's full phone number every time, you simply tap their saved contact. Method references similarly point directly to an existing method instead of rewriting its invocation.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Method References, Lambda Expressions, Functional Interfaces, Constructor References, Streams API, Predicate, Function, Consumer, Supplier, and the :: operator are common Java interview topics.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Can every lambda be replaced with a method reference?
items.answer: No. Only lambdas that directly call an existing method without additional logic can be replaced.

items.question: Does a method reference execute immediately?
items.answer: No. It simply provides a reference that is invoked when the functional interface method is called.

items.question: Can constructor references create objects?
items.answer: Yes. Constructor references use the ::new syntax to instantiate objects.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Method references provide a concise way to reuse existing methods with functional interfaces by using the :: operator.
